theme: Tiny Shifts That Change Your Life

feed.author: Daniel Kahneman
feed.hook: You trust your confidence too much.
feed.body: Feeling certain is not proof of being right.
feed.micro_explanation: The mind often mistakes confidence for accuracy.

feed.author: James Clear
feed.hook: Your future hides inside your ordinary days.
feed.body: Tiny repeated actions quietly become identity.
feed.micro_explanation: Habits compound long before results become visible.

feed.author: Morgan Housel
feed.body: Excitement and good financial decisions rarely travel together.
feed.micro_explanation: Long-term wealth usually grows through patience, not adrenaline.

feed.author: Marcus Aurelius
feed.body: “We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.”
feed.micro_explanation: The mind rehearses pain long before life delivers it.

feed.author: Cal Newport
feed.body: Every interruption quietly steals thinking momentum.
feed.micro_explanation: Focus is expensive because rebuilding it takes time.

feed.author: Robert Cialdini
feed.hook: People copy more than they think.
feed.body: Much of behavior is imitation disguised as choice.
feed.micro_explanation: Humans look to others when uncertainty appears.

feed.author: Viktor Frankl
feed.hook: Pain changes shape when meaning appears.
feed.body: Hardship feels lighter when it points somewhere.
feed.micro_explanation: Purpose changes how suffering is experienced.

feed.author: Yuval Noah Harari
feed.hook: Money works because strangers believe together.
feed.body: Civilizations scaled when humans trusted shared stories.
feed.micro_explanation: Belief systems helped millions coordinate peacefully.

feed.author: Twyla Tharp
feed.body: Creative people often depend on boring rituals.
feed.micro_explanation: Consistency frees mental energy for originality.

feed.author: Nassim Taleb
feed.hook: Luck wears the costume of skill.
feed.body: A good outcome does not always mean a good decision.
feed.micro_explanation: Short-term success can hide bad judgment.

feed.author: Robert Greene
feed.body: Character hides in repeated small behaviors.
feed.micro_explanation: Patterns often matter more than promises.

feed.source: Modern Man in Search of a Soul
feed.author: Carl Jung
feed.hook: What you ignore quietly controls you.
feed.body: Avoided emotions do not disappear. They wait.

feed.author: Alice Schroeder
feed.body: Much of his edge came from quiet accumulation of ideas.

feed.author: Charlie Munger
feed.body: Instead of asking how to win, ask how to fail.
feed.micro_explanation: Avoiding stupidity is often easier than finding brilliance.

feed.author: Greg McKeown
feed.body: Every commitment quietly spends future attention.
feed.micro_explanation: Focus grows when unnecessary obligations shrink.
